title: Coordinate polarization
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ and let $i$ be a coordinate. The polarization of $f$ at $i$ takes, at an input with $i$th coordinate $1$, the maximum of the two values of $f$ obtained by setting that coordinate to $1$ and $-1$; at an input with $i$th coordinate $-1$, it takes their minimum. For a finite list of coordinates, successive polarization means applying these operations in list order, with the empty list leaving $f$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
A finite list of coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}
